article_context: 讨论深度阅读为何不能单靠时间管理技巧获得，并批判把时间纯粹视为效率资源的心态，主张通过仪式化阅读进入更沉浸的“灵魂时间”。

article.title: 阅读 Text 3 · 为什么“挤时间”不等于真正阅读
article.background: 讨论深度阅读为何不能单靠时间管理技巧获得，并批判把时间纯粹视为效率资源的心态，主张通过仪式化阅读进入更沉浸的“灵魂时间”。

sentences.en: That everyone's too busy these days is a cliché.
sentences.zh: 如今人人都太忙，已经成了陈词滥调。

segments.text: That everyone's too busy these days is a cliché.

sentences.en: But one specific complaint is made especially mournfully: There's never any time to read.
sentences.zh: 但有一种抱怨尤其带着惆怅：再也没有时间读书了。

segments.text: But one specific complaint is made especially mournfully: There's never any time to read.

sentences.en: What makes the problem thornier is that the usual time-management techniques don't seem sufficient.
sentences.zh: 问题更棘手之处在于，通常的时间管理技巧似乎并不足够。

segments.text: What makes the problem thornier is that the usual time-management techniques don't seem sufficient.

sentences.en: The web's full of articles offering tips on making time to read: "Give up TV" or "Carry a book with you at all times."
sentences.zh: 网上到处都是教人如何挤出阅读时间的文章，比如“别看电视”或“随身带一本书”。

segments.text: The web's full of articles offering tips on making time to read: "Give up TV" or "Carry a book with you at all times."

sentences.en: But in my experience, using such methods to free up the odd 30 minutes doesn't work.
sentences.zh: 但依我的经验，用这些办法零零碎碎腾出30分钟并不奏效。

segments.text: But in my experience, using such methods to free up the odd 30 minutes doesn't work.

sentences.en: Sit down to read and the flywheel of work-related thoughts keeps spinning - or else you're so exhausted that a challenging book's the last thing you need.
sentences.zh: 你坐下来读书时，脑中与工作有关的念头仍像飞轮一样不停转动；或者你已经疲惫不堪，根本不想碰一本有难度的书。

segments.text: Sit down to read and the flywheel of work-related thoughts keeps spinning - or else you're so exhausted that a challenging book's the last thing you need.

sentences.en: The modern mind, Tim Parks, a novelist and critic, writes, "is overwhelmingly inclined toward communication... It is not simply that one is interrupted; it is that one is actually inclined to interruption."
sentences.zh: 小说家兼评论家蒂姆·帕克斯写道，现代人的心智“极度倾向于沟通……问题不只是我们被打断，而是我们实际上主动倾向于被打断”。

segments.text: The modern mind, Tim Parks, a novelist and critic, writes, "is overwhelmingly inclined toward communication... It is not simply that one is interrupted; it is that one is actually inclined to interruption."

sentences.en: Deep reading requires not just time, but a special kind of time which can't be obtained merely by becoming more efficient.
sentences.zh: 深度阅读需要的不只是时间，而是一种特殊性质的时间；仅仅提高效率并不能获得它。

segments.text: Deep reading requires not just time, but a special kind of time which can't be obtained merely by becoming more efficient.

sentences.en: In fact, "becoming more efficient" is part of the problem.
sentences.zh: 事实上，“变得更高效”本身就是问题的一部分。

segments.text: In fact, "becoming more efficient" is part of the problem.

sentences.en: Thinking of time as a resource to be maximised means you approach it instrumentally, judging any given moment as well spent only in so far as it advances progress toward some goal.
sentences.zh: 把时间视为一种需要最大化利用的资源，意味着你会以工具性的眼光对待时间：只有某一刻推动你朝某个目标前进时，你才觉得它没有被浪费。

segments.text: Thinking of time as a resource to be maximised means you approach it instrumentally, judging any given moment as well spent only in so far as it advances progress toward some goal.

sentences.en: Immersive reading, by contrast, depends on being willing to risk inefficiency, goallessness, even time-wasting.
sentences.zh: 相比之下，沉浸式阅读要求人愿意承担低效率、无目标，甚至“浪费时间”的风险。

segments.text: Immersive reading, by contrast, depends on being willing to risk inefficiency, goallessness, even time-wasting.

sentences.en: Try to slot it in as a to-do list item and you'll manage only goal-focused reading - useful, sometimes, but not the most fulfilling kind.
sentences.zh: 如果把阅读硬塞进待办事项清单，你最终只能进行目标导向型阅读——这种阅读有时很有用，却并非最令人满足的那一种。

segments.text: Try to slot it in as a to-do list item and you'll manage only goal-focused reading - useful, sometimes, but not the most fulfilling kind.

sentences.en: "The future comes at us like empty bottles along an unstoppable and nearly infinite conveyor belt," writes Gary Eberle in his book Sacred Time, and "we feel a pressure to fill these different-sized bottles (days, hours, minutes) as they pass, for if they get by without being filled, we will have wasted them."
sentences.zh: 加里·埃伯勒在《神圣的时间》中写道：“未来像一个个空瓶子，沿着一条不可阻挡、近乎无限的传送带向我们驶来。”我们因此“感到一种压力，要在这些大小不同的瓶子——日、时、分——经过时把它们装满，因为如果它们空着溜走，我们就会觉得自己浪费了它们”。

segments.text: "The future comes at us like empty bottles along an unstoppable and nearly infinite conveyor belt," writes Gary Eberle in his book Sacred Time, and "we feel a pressure to fill these different-sized bottles (days, hours, minutes) as they pass, for if they get by without being filled, we will have wasted them."

sentences.en: No mind-set could be worse for losing yourself in a book.
sentences.zh: 若想沉浸在一本书中，没有什么心态比这更糟。

segments.text: No mind-set could be worse for losing yourself in a book.

sentences.en: So what does work?
sentences.zh: 那么，什么办法真正有效？

segments.text: So what does work?

sentences.en: Perhaps surprisingly, scheduling regular times for reading.
sentences.zh: 也许出人意料：给阅读固定安排规律的时间。

segments.text: Perhaps surprisingly, scheduling regular times for reading.

sentences.en: You'd think this might fuel the efficiency mind-set, but in fact, Eberle notes, such ritualistic behaviour helps us "step outside time's flow" into "soul time."
sentences.zh: 你可能以为这会强化效率至上的心态，但埃伯勒指出，这种带有仪式感的行为反而能帮助我们“走出时间之流”，进入“灵魂时间”。

segments.text: You'd think this might fuel the efficiency mind-set, but in fact, Eberle notes, such ritualistic behaviour helps us "step outside time's flow" into "soul time."

sentences.en: You could limit distractions by reading only physical books, or on single-purpose e-readers.
sentences.zh: 你也可以只读纸质书，或使用功能单一的电子阅读器，以减少干扰。

segments.text: You could limit distractions by reading only physical books, or on single-purpose e-readers.

sentences.en: "Carry a book with you at all times" can actually work, too - providing you dip in often enough, so that reading becomes the default state from which you temporarily surface to take care of business, before dropping back down.
sentences.zh: “随身带一本书”其实也能奏效——前提是你足够频繁地读它，让阅读成为默认状态；你只是暂时浮出水面处理事务，然后再沉回书中。

segments.text: "Carry a book with you at all times" can actually work, too - providing you dip in often enough, so that reading becomes the default state from which you temporarily surface to take care of business, before dropping back down.

sentences.en: On a really good day, it no longer feels as if you're "making time to read," but just reading, and making time for everything else.
sentences.zh: 在真正美好的一天里，你不再觉得自己是在“挤时间读书”，而只是自然地阅读，并为其他一切事情挤出时间。

segments.text: On a really good day, it no longer feels as if you're "making time to read," but just reading, and making time for everything else.
